title: Japanese Prime Minister Leaves India with Key Agreements
main_content:
Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe ended his three-day visit to India last Sunday, where he signed a number of agreements in key areas.

The two countries sealed their warming ties with a deal for Tokyo to build India’s first high-speed train, defense pacts that will clear the way for Japan to sell weapons to India, and progress on a civil nuclear agreement.

The deals were announced following a meeting between Abe and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi.

The two nationalist leaders share a close rapport, and the economic and security partnership between the two countries has received a major boost since Modi came to power last year.

Abe described the agreements as heralding a new era of cooperation between the two countries. He said “strong India is for the good of Japan and strong Japan is good for India, this is my basic tenet.”

Japan will provide $12 billion to build a bullet train that will run between the western cities of Mumbai and Ahmedabad. Modi, who has been looking to Tokyo to pump in capital to overhaul the country’s infrastructure, said “this enterprise will launch a revolution in India’s railways and speed up India’s journey into the future.”

Explaining why India deeply values the strategic partnership with Japan, Modi said, “No friend will matter more in realizing India’s economic dreams than Japan and I cannot think of a strategic partnership that can exercise a more profound influence on shaping the course of Asia and our interlinked ocean regions more than ours.”

questions.question: What agreements did Japan and India come to?
options: A deal for Japan to supply oil to India
A deal for Tokyo to build India’s first high-speed train and defense pacts
An agreement for India to export textiles to Japan
A collaboration on technology sharing between Japan and India
questions.answer: A deal for Tokyo to build India’s first high-speed train and defense pacts

questions.question: What helped boost the relations between India and Japan?
options: The close rapport between Abe and Modi and mutual economic interests
Joint military exercises and trade tariffs
questions.answer: The close rapport between Abe and Modi and mutual economic interests

questions.question: What is Shinzo Abe’s opinion about the agreements?
options: He believes they are only beneficial for Japan
He sees them as a minor step in Japan's foreign policy
He describes them as heralding a new era of cooperation
He thinks they will not significantly impact India's economy
questions.answer: He describes them as heralding a new era of cooperation
